venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Same first step. Different answer. Baugh is the night. Woods is the lever. The hitch is the tax.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — condensed sit with Charles plus GNFP Week 2 (Di Virgilio film pass, Sep 7). Fan rail stays empty until Charles approves.
headline: Faulkner dresses the line so you cannot sit on Baugh. White moves Woods so the tackle never gets a clean count. FAU still lived on the throw Florida left on the grass.

offense.body:
The picture keeps changing. The answers stay simple. Baugh is the night. The line is how they keep you from sitting on him.

They start from their own 6 after Coleman’s pick. Two tight ends, H-back off the line. Read. Give. Baugh, 9. Next snap, same family. The line washes right. Baugh cuts left, 8. Same play, other hole.

Then they lie to you. Brown in motion, four yards deep. Tackles pull like it is counter. The interior three release the other way. The ball goes to Brown — to the three, not the pullers. FAU stepped with the pullers. That is the design.

They show pistol once in the opening script. H-back, three wide. Run on second-and-2. Same set, play-action, Wilson sits under the zone, 19. Pistol is one look. It is not the offense.

Motion, counter, keep: tackles one way, motion the other. The end crashes. Philo keeps it. Sledge is still there. Minus 2. The design was sound. FAU won the snap.

Then the throw that starts the Sumrall era. Corners off. They will not come down for Baugh. Hitch to Brown on the backside — the side the line is not selling. Catch at the 50. First man misses. Forty-nine yards. People will remember the score. The play is five yards, on time, after they refused the run.

That is the night in one series. Same first step. Different answer.

What the rest of the tape is doing

Faulkner does not need a new play. He changes who you have to count.

They split them out wide and stack Brown and Wilson behind the two in front. FAU keeps extra in the box because they have seen Baugh. That leaves one-on-one with a lot of grass. One miss is a house call. The 49 lives there. So does the rest of Brown’s night — the screen, the 14, the 33, the 18. He is not a gadget.

They load one side, then motion, and the strength moves. FAU’s count is late. They can still go the other way without a new call. The backside is live. Sumrall said it Monday: every blade of grass.

The pull is sometimes the lie and sometimes the truth. Tackles sell counter, interior three leave, ball goes with the three — Brown, later Clark. Clark’s 10-yard score is that family with the big people already down the field. When the pull is real, Baugh hits it from 12 and the pullers lead. When they need a yard, nobody leaves — sneak on fourth-and-1, Philo from the 3.

They will also pull the tackle on a pass. The end is paid to rush the passer. Instead the tackle leaves like the run is going the other way. If the end just runs the quarterback, you are in trouble. If you honor it, the front slows down without getting blocked. Week one they plant that look more than they cash it. They will hand it out of the same picture. Remember it.

When they crowd the run, the line is in a pass set. Abrams, 63, over the top. That shot only exists because Baugh was real.

Wilson moves the chains all night — 19, 15, 13. He sits where the zone leaves him. Stockton catches at the 11, a ball that is a touch late, and he walks in. Philo is in command. Eyes down when the rush comes. He does not have to be the hero. When he holds it, the play dies — the ball off Mays, Sweeney sitting.

Baugh is 14 for 160 and three rushing scores, and the 61 when the whole stadium knows. Eight or nine times FAU fills the gaps — the right call — and he still rips it or scores. That is not scheme winning those snaps. That is the best player in the building. Faulkner’s job is to keep you from putting eleven on him.

Downfield they block like they mean it. Micah Jones late: he blows up the end, then the next guy, and they throw him the last one. That is not a coincidence. Get the big people in front of a skill player, or get the skill player to finish the block. Same idea.

What to clean

The keep when Sledge crashes and is still there.
The snap that loses twenty inside the five. Sumrall already tied the high snaps to a run-block that messes with Moore’s hands. Technique. They know.
The ball off Mays.
Outside zone they cannot run yet. Faulkner will still put it on film so you have to honor the edge. Do not confuse that with who they are.

The line is not road-grading anybody. They are clean — no hold, no false start parade, the late shift that wrecked them last year does not get them. Faulkner’s hack is he does not ask them to win every one-on-one. He leaves people unblocked and lets Baugh and the picture do the rest.
bullets: Same first step, different answer: the screen, the punch, the sneak.
Tackles sell counter. Interior three leave. Ball goes with the three — Brown, later Clark.
When the pull is real, Baugh hits it. When they need a yard, nobody leaves.
Abrams 63 is the pass set. Clean the Sledge keep, the snap, and the ball off Mays.

defense.body:
White’s defense is odd fronts, movement, and disguising the JACK. He mixes looks often — not every snap — enough that FAU’s line never gets a clean count.

Woods is the lever. On third down White moves him. On the ball, he is the edge. Off the ball, the edge belongs to somebody else and Woods is coming or dropping from a different spot. That is a better rush lane without telling the tackle who has him.

Third-and-7, FAU 28: Woods in a backer, press, comeback to Henry, McClain, they convert.
Third-and-1, FAU 47: Woods off, nickel on the line, corners off, hitch to Valsin, Hanks, they convert.
First-and-10 at the Florida 46: 3-3-5, corners off, one-high. Tillman, 3, Chiles fills. They win the snap.
Second-and-7: still 3-3-5, the front changes — tackles spaced, both edges up, stunt. Valsin, 8, Hanks, convert.

That throw is the tax. White will live with five-to-eight yards if they tackle. FAU lived there for 90 snaps. They were 10-of-13 on third at one point because nobody sat in the window. The corners are off. The backers are not fanning into the hitch. You showed them something before the snap and then you gave them the first read. Sumrall said it. Third-and-1, you cannot play nine yards off.

The payoff when he holds it

Third-and-10 at the Florida 35. Shade front — three down to one side. Press one way, off the other. Coleman opens to the middle, sells the hole, the ball goes outside, Coleman is already back. That is the pick. Not a blitz. He moved the quarterback’s eyes. Messer tackles him on the return.

Johnson’s pick is the same family. Coleman tips it. First snap after a Baugh score. He held it. They took it.

Bett later knives the keep at the 1. Ball out. Johnson falls on it. The rush finally finishes.

McCloud takes fourth-and-2. James stops Ervin to end the half. Chiles on the short middle. Those are the snaps that look like the plan.

What leaked

Henry and Valsin taking what was given.
The pile at the 1. The front was right. They lost the yard.
The edge leaving and Veltkamp walking in from 7. Woods is the lever — and a handful of times he does not set the edge. New guy, a little hot. FAU ran at him.
The fade when the corner is off. Valsin, 20. Same play Stockton ran the other way. Clark at STAR played a huge night and lost that one with no help over the top.
Hoch on fourth down.

The later condensed cut is mostly four-down, corners off, one-high. That is how they play the explosive. That is also how the hitch and the fade stay alive. Safeties were the clean room — Coleman, Thornton. The corners were the plan and the leak.

Sumrall called it atrocious at times. He is not wrong. Veltkamp is a real small-school quarterback. Ninety snaps is what happens when you give him the short one and do not climb.

Sit on the hitch. Keep the edge when the quarterback keeps it. Mix Woods. Do not park him, and do not leave him on an island if he is going to chase.
bullets: 3-3-5, spaced, shaded. Woods is the lever on third down.
Coleman sells middle, takes outside. Johnson’s pick is the same family.
They play off a lot. The hitch is the tax because nobody sat in the window. Ninety snaps.
Clean the pile, the edge, the fade, Hoch on fourth.

specials.body: The drive stalls. They take the points. Durkin from 53. Florida never punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt is how the second Florida score starts.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt sets up the short field.

keys: Offense: sequenced. Same first step, different answer. FAU never gets set. Baugh is the night.
Defense: odd fronts, Woods on third down, disguise. Not every snap. Often.
The hitch is the tax because nobody sat in the window.
Florida’s payoff: make him hold it. Coleman’s pick.

nextWeek.look: They will throw it short and keep it. Sixkiller is the show — he throws it and he is their leading runner. Florida will still run Baugh and dress the line — pullers one way, interior the other. White has to sit on the hitch and keep Woods’ edge home when the quarterback pulls it.
